name: Praziquantel
route_note: oral tablets, often as a single dose (or one day's doses) with food; dispersible arpraziquantel for young children
originator: Bayer and E. Merck (Merck KGaA), Germany
owner: generic (many); Merck KGaA donates tablets to WHO

discovery.by: Bayer and E. Merck research laboratories
discovery.note: Discovered in a joint programme on pyrazinoisoquinolines; its anthelmintic activity was established in the mid-1970s, first in veterinary medicine.

tagline: The single drug behind schistosomiasis control across Africa
summary: Praziquantel is the main drug against schistosomiasis and is also used for liver flukes and tapeworm infections. A single day's treatment causes rapid paralysis and damage to the worms' outer surface. Merck KGaA donates hundreds of millions of tablets a year for mass treatment of school-age children, and a child-friendly formulation of its active enantiomer (arpraziquantel) was approved in 2023–2024.
mechanism: Praziquantel activates a transient receptor potential channel of the melastatin family in schistosomes and other flatworms (TRPM_PZQ), which was identified as its target around 2019–2021. The resulting rapid calcium influx causes spastic muscle paralysis.

It also damages the worm's tegument (outer surface), exposing parasite antigens to the immune system. The (R)-enantiomer carries the activity; immature schistosomes are relatively insensitive, which is one reason for repeat treatment.
uses: Liver fluke infections: clonorchiasis and opisthorchiasis

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Praziquantel is synthesised in the Bayer–Merck collaboration.

history.title: Human schistosomiasis
history.detail: Praziquantel enters human use for schistosomiasis in the early 1980s, replacing more toxic drugs.

history.title: Donation
history.detail: Merck KGaA begins donating praziquantel to WHO, later expanding to up to 250 million tablets per year.

history.title: Target identified
history.detail: Studies by Marchant and colleagues show that praziquantel activates the schistosome TRPM_PZQ channel.

history.title: Paediatric arpraziquantel
history.detail: The EMA gives a positive scientific opinion on arpraziquantel dispersible tablets for children aged 3 months to 6 years, developed by the Pediatric Praziquantel Consortium; WHO prequalification follows in 2024.

pk.bioavailability: well absorbed but extensive first-pass metabolism; increased by food

serious: neurological reactions in neurocysticercosis due to inflammation around dying cysts

facts: Rifampicin is contraindicated with praziquantel because it can reduce praziquantel levels to ineffective concentrations.
Its bitter taste and large tablets prompted the development of the paediatric arpraziquantel formulation.
